identity.title: ALMA unveils rings and gaps in the protoplanetary system <ASTROBJ>HD 169142</ASTROBJ>: signatures of two giant protoplanets

paper_type_evidence.quote: This paper reports new ALMA observations of the dust continuum at 1.3 mm, $^{12}$CO, $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O $J=2-1$ emission from the ( almost face-on) system HD 169142

evidence.quote: The most recent measurement of the parallax is $\varpi = 8.53 \pm 0.29$ mas (cite: Brown16) which translates to a distance $d = 117 \pm 4\,$pc.

question.value: What are the gas and dust surface density structures of HD 169142 (cavity, gap, rings), and do they indicate planets shaping the disk?

evidence.quote: From these observations we place more stringent constraints on the dust and gas density structures.
as part of project 2013.1.00592.S
with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) in band 6 (211–275 GHz)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: USB: 233 GHz TDM continuum (2 GHz) and 12CO FDM (0.040 km/s); LSB: 13CO and C18O FDM (0.084 km/s)

evidence.quote: The upper sideband (USB) contained two spectral windows.
Each observed LSB line had a frequency (velocity) resolution of 61.0 kHz (0.084 km s$^{-1}$).
with 2 GHz bandwidth centered at 233 GHz
35 antennas were used to achieve a spatial resolution of $\sim 0.2\ensuremath{''} - 0.3\ensuremath{''}$
for 50 minutes total on-source

flux_calibrator.value: Ceres (1.941 Jy LSB, 2.165 Jy USB); J1924-2914 bandpass; J1812-2836 gain

evidence.quote: Calibration was done with $J1924-2914$ as the delay and bandpass calibrator, J1812-2836 as the gain calibrator, and Ceres as the flux calibrator.

self_calibration.value: Two phase and one amplitude; first phase solint 300 s; reference antenna DA59; solutions from TDM window applied to FDM windows

evidence.quote: Calibration solutions were calculated twice for phase and once for amplitude.
Data reduction was performed with the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA, (cite: Mcmullin07)).

evidence.quote: Continuum subtraction of the line data was done in $uv-$space based on a single-order polynomial fit to all line-free channels in each spectral window.

evidence.quote: The fiducial model is defined by the set of parameters that minimise the difference between observations and model grid within the explored parameter space.

results_numeric.quantity: Dust mass upper limit in gap

evidence.quote: This corresponds to a dust mass 3 $\sigma$ upper limit of $\sim$ 0.3 M$_{\oplus}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Dust mass upper limit in cavity

evidence.quote: is $\sim 10^{-2}$ M$_{\oplus}$
The total dust mass is $1 \times 10^{-4}\,$M$_{\odot}$.
The total gas mass is $1.9 \times 10^{-2}\,$M$_{\odot}$

results_numeric.quantity: Gas surface density reduction inward of dust gap

evidence.quote: The gas surface density inward of the dust gap is decreased by a factor of $\sim$ 30 – 40
down to an inner radius of $\sim 13\,$au
The outer gas radius of 180 au is set by the steep drop of the C$^{18}$O emission at large radii.
The inner ring is decreased by a factor of $\sim 3.7$ (=$1/\delta_{\rm dust}$)

findings_qualitative.value: Dust is in two rings (20-35 au and 56-83 au) with no dust in cavity or gap, while gas is present inside and extends to ~180 au, indicating radial drift and decoupling

evidence.quote: gas and dust in HD 169142 are physically decoupled with the dust particles concentrated in two rings between $\sim 20 - 35$ au and $\sim 56-83$ au.

claims.hypothesis: Are the dust cavity and gap real dust depletions with gas remaining?
claims.experiment: 1.3 mm continuum and CO isotopologue imaging plus DALI modelling
claims.result: No dust above noise in cavity/gap; gas reduced by 30-40 inward of the gap
claims.finding: Gas filled gap and cavity with depleted surface density

evidence.quote: The dust cavity and gap are filled in with gas as suggested by the emission maps of the three CO isotopologues

claims.hypothesis: Do the structures indicate multiple giant planets?
claims.experiment: Compare gas/dust structures and absence of asymmetries with planet-disk theory
claims.result: Inferred planet masses ~0.1-1 MJup inner and ~1-10 MJup outer
claims.finding: Two giant planets most likely scenario; MRI dead zone plus wind alternative not excluded

evidence.quote: the ALMA data presented here are consistent with the presence of two giant planets

claims.hypothesis: Does the dust disk being smaller than the gas disk imply radial drift?
claims.experiment: Compare continuum and CO radial extents
claims.result: Dust edge at 83 au, gas to ~180 au
claims.finding: Sharp dust edge hints at radial drift

evidence.quote: The sharp edge of the continuum map at 83 au is indicative of radial drift of dust grains

why_this_method.value: Multiple CO isotopologues with different optical depths allow detection of small gas amounts in the gap

evidence.quote: thanks to the different optical depths, the spatially resolved channel maps of the three isotopologues allows us to detect and quantify the very small amount

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: MRI dead zones with photoevaporation or MHD wind could also explain the structure

evidence.quote: An alternative scenario that could also explain the surface density profile of HD 169142 is the case of magneto-rotational (MRI) instability creating dead-zones

limitations_admitted.value: Azimuthal asymmetries are low significance (<~3 sigma); model 13CO flux underestimated ~10%

evidence.quote: The significance of the asymmetric emission along the minor axis (continuum and C$^{18}$O) is low ($\lesssim 3\sigma$)

referee_caveats_inferred: Grid fit has no formal uncertainties or degeneracy exploration
Fixed dust opacity and gas-to-dust ratio assumptions affect masses
Resolution (~35 au) limits gap and cavity constraints
